tools.description:
Use this tool when the user asks to see client reviews for a specific service provider (company).

It returns detailed reviews that include project information, pricing, scope, client feedback, ratings,
 and more.
Optionally filter reviews by a specific service.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "send_message_to_provider" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Reach out to a service provider to get a quote, discuss project needs, explore a partnership, find a job, etc. This tool sends the SAME message to one or more p…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_provider_info, get_service_provider_reviews, recommend_service_providers, send_message_to_provider · Public sink: send_message_to_provider.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_provider_info, get_service_provider_reviews, recommend_service_providers, send_message_to_provider · Public sink: send_message_to_provider

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "recommend_service_providers" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
